newsitem.title: USA: Dlr surges against Europe on Swiss comments, Yeltsin worries.
newsitem.headline: Dlr surges against Europe on Swiss comments, Yeltsin worries.

text.p: The dollar climbed sharply against the Swiss franc and rose to its highest level in over two and a half years against the German mark on Monday, after a Swiss official said he was content with recent weakness in his country's currency.

The dollar's impressive performance against European currencies helped it regain its footing against the yen. After retreating from a near four year high versus the Japanese currency on Friday, the dollar resumed its climb on Monday, once again nearing the key 120 level.

"The dollar has come back very well," said Russell LaScala, head of the spot trading desk at Citibank. "People sold the Swiss franc on the comments out of Switzerland and the dollar was dragged higher against the mark as well."

After reaching a peak of 1.6493 marks, its highest level since June 1994, the dollar ended the day at 1.6475 marks, significantly higher than Friday's close of 1.6288. The dollar surged to a close of 1.4295 Swiss francs, over two centimes higher than Friday's close of 1.4060.
Swiss Finance Minister Kaspar Villiger said Monday he was "relieved" by the weak Swiss franc, prompting a flood of franc sales, which boosted the dollar against a host of European currencies.

Dealers said the remarks were consistent with recent efforts on the part of the Swiss central bank to push the franc lower as a means of jump-starting the sluggish Swiss economy. A weaker currency tends to boost a country's exports by making them less less expensive abroad.
The dollar's good tone against Europe, and in particular against the mark, was also helped by renewed fears about the health of Russian President Boris Yeltsin.

On Monday, a Kremlin spokesman said doctors had advised the 65-year old leader, who is recovering from pneumonia and has not been seen in public for three weeks, not to leave Moscow. A scheduled trip to the Netherlands, where Yeltsin was to have met Dutch Prime Minister Wim Kok on February 4, was cancelled.
Because of the close economic ties between the two countries, the German mark tends to suffer when political uncertainty in Russia surfaces.

The dollar also performed well against the yen, but dealers were hesitant to push it too high after talk last week that the Japanese central bank had been defending the yen near the 120 level. On Friday, the dollar reached 120.15 yen, its highest level in 47 months, before retreating on the rumours.

"Although everyone is bullish on the dollar I think it's harder to be as bullish on the dollar against the yen because of the psychological 120 level," said Lizbeth Goldberg, assistant vice president on the foreign exchange desk at Bayerische Hypotheken und Wechselbank in New York.
"As soon as we got to 120 last week there were all sorts of rumours about the Bank of Japan," she added.
The dollar ended the day at 119.43 yen, up from 118.90 on Friday.
Elsewhere, sterling retreated against the dollar, closing at $1.6225 against $1.6293. The dollar retreated modestly to close at Canadian $1.3442 against $1.3488 on Friday.
